items.headline: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
items.blurb: Pressures weighed on US markets, with the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed into correction territory.
items.text: Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off dragged markets down. The sell-off comes as concerns remain over the speed and size of artificial intelligence investment, but also as some large companies including Nvidia and SpaceX faced specific issues that worried investors. Those pressures combined to weigh on US markets through Friday, with all key US indexes closing sharply down on the day, furthering earlier falls over the week. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were pushed into correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high. The S&P 500 closed down 3.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index plunged 5.3%. However, all three indexes were up on where they were a year ago. items.headline: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
items.blurb: Copenhagen accuses Moscow of planning assassination with banned local gang; Russia says no evidence for allegation.
items.text: Denmark has said it is expelling Russia’s defence attaché after accusing Moscow intelligence of plotting to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen. “We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attaché from Denmark” within seven days, Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference on Friday. The expulsion ultimatum comes hours after Denmark’s intelligence agency, PET, said it suspected Russia of planning the assassination during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb with help of a Danish gang. Danish public broadcaster DR named the rapper as Kyivstoner, who has both Ukrainian and US citizenship. “A Russian assassination attempt is not something we’ve seen in Denmark before, and that gives me an impression of an increasingly aggressive and risk-taking Russia,” PET head Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen told journalists on Friday. “The case shows, in our assessment, that the Russian intelligence services attempted to carry out an execution in Denmark,” he said. items.headline: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.blurb: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities.
items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.headline: UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal, says Burnham
items.blurb: The UK-EU deal agreed on Friday covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.
items.text: Andy Burnham said the UK will discuss possible options for even closer ties with the EU, after agreeing a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. The prime minister said it was a "good day" for Britain and Europe, adding the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to £17bn a year. European Council President António Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people". Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the UK Parliament next week. Burnham arrived in Brussels to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU, which originally began under former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer. The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028. items.headline: Can Mauricio Pochettino save Man United from Premier League relegation?
items.blurb: Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United for the first time on Sunday, in a trip to rivals Liverpool.
items.text: Manchester United will be led by a third manager in three years when Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first match since replacing Michael Carrick . The fact that the Premier League clash is against their fierce rivals Liverpool – the team that, with United, are joint record English top-flight champions – is an added twist to a sordid recent tale for the Manchester club. When Sir Alex Ferguson retired after lifting a then-record 20th league title in 2013, the Red Devils had climbed to the biggest and richest club in the world. Now, apart from not being able to claim a Premier League crown since 2013, they are laden with debt – and worse still, they sit inside the relegation zone. The last time United were relegated from the top flight was in the 1973–1974 season. That came only six years after one of the club’s greatest nights – the lifting of the European Cup (now the Champions League), making them the first English club to do so. items.headline: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.headline: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
items.blurb: Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.
items.text: Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region. Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow. Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border. The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact". items.headline: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
items.blurb: Police say two children among dead as search continues for more victims.
items.text: A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of people to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least four people, according to police. The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, police spokesperson Musa Mohammed told the Reuters news agency. Police said 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic, and five taken to a hospital in the state capital. Search teams were still looking for more victims, police said. Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told Reuters there were at least 300. Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody. According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district. The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”. Such boat accidents

items.headline: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.blurb: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
items.text: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). items.headline: French police officers sentenced for beating of music producer Michel Zecler
items.blurb: The court has upheld the 2020 beating of the black music producer as an aggravated circumstance of racism.
items.text: Three French police officers have been convicted of beating up a black music producer six years ago in Paris in what the court upheld as an aggravated circumstance of racism. The three were also found guilty of signing a falsified police report stating that the producer - Michel Zecler, 47 - had violently resisted their attempt to arrest him. Their lies were exposed because the whole scene at Zecler's recording studio was caught on CCTV, revealing the producer had suffered some 30 punches, kicks and baton strikes while offering little resistance at all. Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, Philippe Tondeux, 50, and Pierre Plantier, 37, all received five year sentences, with different amounts suspended. Lapersonne had three years of his sentence suspended and Tondeux three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended, and will serve his one year with an ankle monitor. The case became a cause célèbre for critics of the police, who say it exposed systematic racism among officers. Right now at Shija, we have 150 patients who have come for tests, and many more patients are also at Babina undergoing the same treatment. This is a very unfortunate incident, but with the support that we received today from our honourable CM, we are very happy with the financial assistance that he has assured us,” Langhu, a village head, was quoted as saying by ANI. He added: “In the last two to three days, we came across this outbreak. From the source that I received, it is basically from consuming liquor . items.headline: Bengal CEO puts summary voter roll revision on hold
items.blurb: The delay leaves new and first-time voters uncertain about registration dates and comes as millions of appeals over voter deletions remain pending.
items.text: The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Friday postponed the special summary revision (SSR) of voter list and the publication of draft roll due to “unavoidable circumstances”, sparking a controversy in a state where the special intensive revision (SIR) disenfranchised 2.71 million people earlier this year. The surprise move comes roughly a month after the Election Commission of India (ECI) ordered SSR in 17 states and Union territories, the first such exercise in nearly two years that was expected to not only help Gen Z and first-time voters but also those deleted by SIR. The SSR is already underway in 24 regions, including Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, and Kerala. Bengal is the only province where the exercise was halted. The SSR was scheduled to start on November 23 in the eastern state. “The upcoming program of special summary revision of photo-electoral roll which was scheduled from November 23 onwards is hereby postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances. items.headline: Nvidia Employees Complained About Huang’s Behavior Years Ago
items.blurb: About two decades ago, two Nvidia Corp. employees complained about how then-Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang treated his staff, including allegations that he threatened them and made sexually explicit remarks, according to allegations contained in a California lawsuit filed in 2007.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- About two decades ago, two Nvidia Corp. employees complained about how then-Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang treated his staff, including allegations that he threatened them and made sexually explicit remarks, according to allegations contained in a California lawsuit filed in 2007. Stephen Pettigrew, the first in-house lawyer hired by Nvidia, said he observed Huang regularly verbally abusing and intimidating employees, according to court documents filed in the Superior Court of California. Pettigrew alleged he was fired for raising concerns about the conduct of Nvidia executives, while the company cited performance issues for his termination, according to court documents. “He would scream at them, threaten them with extreme bodily harm and make sexually oriented comments while thrusting his hips in a demonstration of the sex act,” according to a brief filed by Pettigrew’s attorneys in a lawsuit alleging age discrimination and wrongful termination. The dispute, in which Nvidia brought counterclaims against Pettigrew seeking the return of corporate documents, was resolved through a confidential settlement in December 2009. items.blurb: AI investment concerns triggered a broad selloff, pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory and the Nasdaq 100 to its worst week since March 2020. The sharp market pullback reflected worries about slowing data-center construction, tighter AI-project funding and weaker technology earnings growth.
items.text: US stocks took a beating amid fears surrounding artificial intelligence and technology stocks, Bloomberg reported today. Anxiety around viability of AI projects, triggered a full-blown selloff, pushing the Nasdaq 500 to its lowest since the COVID-19 pandemic and the S&P 500 into correction mode. Investors rushed to the safety of bonds and haven currencies amid fears that Wall Street’s biggest investment boom in decades is running out of steam. The S&P 500 equity benchmark down 3.7%, with the index falling for a seventh straight day. The Nasdaq 100 lost 5.6% Friday, posting its worst week since March 2020. Nvidia Corp. sank 14% as Reuters reported US regulators are investigating its accounting practices. Anthropic PBC erased a portion of its first-day surge. A gauge of chipmakers sank 11%. “Smackdown!” said Steve Sosnick at Interactive Brokers. “The problem stems from investors’ rapidly changed perceptions about technology, particularly the pace and cost of the artificial-intelligence buildout.” The resurgence in equity volatility sent the so-called fear gauge to its highest since April 2025. items.headline: Who is Jay Mehta? Meet Juhi Chawla’s husband selling half of his 45% KKR stake for $400 million
items.blurb: Jay Mehta, husband of actor Juhi Chawla and a director of the Mehta Group, is reportedly set to sell half of his 45% stake in Kolkata Knight Riders to US-based Ares Management for $400 million. The deal would value the IPL franchise at around $1.78 billion, subject to BCCI approval.
items.text: Jay Mehta, the businessman and husband of Bollywood actor Juhi Chawla, is in the spotlight after reportedly agreeing to sell half of his stake in Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) to US-based investment management firm Ares Management for approximately $400 million. According to a report by Cricbuzz , Mehta is set to offload a 22.5% stake in the three-time IPL champions, out of his existing 45% holding. The proposed all-cash transaction values KKR at approximately $1.78 billion (around ₹ 16,634 crore). The deal is nearing completion but requires formal approval from the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ). Jay Mahendra Mehta is an Indian businessman who heads the Indian operations of the Mehta Group, a multinational family-owned business headquartered in Mumbai. He is married to actor Juhi Chawla , with whom he has two children. Mehta is the grandson of industrialist Nanji Kalidas Mehta, who established the Mehta Group. The conglomerate has business interests spanning several sectors, including cement and building materials, packaging, sugar, horticulture, engineering, electrical cables, agrochemicals and financial services.

items.blurb: India’s gaming industry is moving beyond gameplay, with live streaming, esports, gaming communities and in-game commerce creating new opportunities for platforms. Companies such as Rooter are looking to capitalise on this growing market by bringing gamers, content creators and publishers onto a single platform.
items.text: India’s gaming industry is moving beyond gameplay, with live streaming, esports, gaming communities and in-game commerce creating new opportunities for platforms. Companies such as Rooter are looking to capitalise on this growing market by bringing gamers, content creators and publishers onto a single platform. Rising mobile gaming adoption and new monetisation avenues have further increased interest in the segment. Founded in 2016 by Piyush Kumar and Dipesh Agarwal, Rooter operates a gaming live-streaming and commerce platform that allows users to stream and watch gameplay across popular titles such as BGMI, Call of Duty and Valorant, while engaging with gaming creators. The company has also entered gaming commerce, selling in-game currencies and gift cards to build a revenue stream beyond advertising and content. Rooter’s strategy appears to be gaining traction, with the company more than doubling its operating revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 78.9 crore in the previous financial year, while narrowing its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr . items.text: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round. The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release. The company also plans to deepen investments in agentic AI and AI co-pilots to improve credit assessment and customer engagement. Founded by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh in 2021, InPrime began operations in 2023. The company is an AI-first non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on India's emerging middle class, particularly customers operating in the informal economy, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour owners, small retailers and micro-entrepreneurs. InPrime uses AI-driven underwriting, data analytics and an on-ground presence to serve customers who often struggle to access formal credit despite owning property and running established businesses. items.headline: Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed champion
items.blurb: Lauren Price dominates Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.
items.text: Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion. Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles. Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing. But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come. Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity. Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness. Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise. The Tokyo gold medal

items.headline: Countdown: From Steinitz to Gukesh: an elite club of kings
items.text: The first World chess championship was played in 1886. Few sporting events could boast of a longer history. After Spencer Gore defeated William Marshall in straight sets to win the title at Wimbledon in 1877, there have been 66 other different champions in the men’s singles. Jannik Sinner, you may recall, became No. 67 four months ago. The club of the World chess champions is a bit more exclusive. As the event turns 140, there have only been 18 members in that club -- when you consider only the undisputed World champions. (And even if you want to add the disputed ones, the number would go up only by four). D. Gukesh, and India, will be hoping that the club would have no further addition, at least for the time being. Javokhir Sindarov, however, can be forgiven if he has enough chances to be crowned the new king on the board of 64 squares. In an extended Stock Market filing to go with their first-quarter financial results that were released on Thursday, United said they would be liable to pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer to hire the Argentine. United announced Pochettino had agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal on 13 November. They borrowed £10m on 16 November. The loan is one of three confirmed after the 30 September first-quarter reporting date, which takes the overall amount owed on their rolling credit limit to £240m. The amount paid to release Pochettino from his USA deal takes the sums paid hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 to £95m. However, that figure is likely to top £100m once the cost of hiring Pochettino's staff and sacking Michael Carrick is added. items.headline: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher’s fusion power startup. Here’s what they’re building.
items.blurb: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
items.text: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant. The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion. Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California. Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations. Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.

A redesign that’s been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely. Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There’s an image generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack . You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey . You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home. items.headline: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.blurb: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.
items.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. items.headline: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
items.blurb: Meta is “re-evaluating” 2030 sustainability goals. Will others follow?
items.text: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report. items.headline: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
items.blurb: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
items.text: The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips? The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue. Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. items.text: On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry's critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech). items.headline: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
items.blurb: Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives.
items.text: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. According to a lawsuit filed by the current and former students, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III, due to “both technological and human errors,” school officials called police to the scene anyway, and the cops responded with force. items.text: Anthropic’s blockbuster listing has put India’s AI ambitions under a harsh spotlight. The IPO has triggered a debate over whether the country can build globally competitive AI companies. So, can India build its own Anthropic before the next AI wave passes it by? The Boardroom Debate: The debate began after Kotak Mahindra Bank founder Uday Kotak said that Anthropic’s $1.5 Tn valuation eclipsed the combined m-cap of India’s ten largest firms. He also questioned whether Indian businesses needed to catch up with the new tech economy. However, ex-Infosys CFO Mohandas Pai urged founders to focus on deeptech R&D to build local champions. But the story is more nuanced than it appears. The Funding Chasm: On paper, India’s AI funding momentum looks brisk. Domestic AI startups raised a record $1.1 Bn in 9M 2026 despite a subdued funding market. Yet much of the funding flowed into vertical AI rather than foundational research as investors steered clear of cash-guzzling LLM startups. Valuation froth isn’t making things any easier. items.headline: Meta to price Muse Charm gadget at $300: The Information
items.blurb: The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference. Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform.

Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, and Enterprise Ireland also participated in the round, along with angel investors like cricketer Rahul Dravid and senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce, and Meta.
